Chapter 251: 0248 Sanguo Sha Selected for the National Online Game Project

"Hello, Director Kou."

"Haha, Xiao Chen, hello to you too. You've done well this year."

"It's all thanks to your support, Director Kou."

On the third day of the ChinaJoy expo, Director Kou from the Publication Administration specifically called Chen Guilang over for a talk.

As early as 12 years ago, when the internet had just appeared in China, Director Kou was already in charge of managing this area. He was also the one who brought ChinaJoy into existence.

In the 1980s, he worked at the National Publishing Bureau, responsible for book publishing. The world-renowned literary works, Japanese manga, and Hong Kong and Taiwan novels introduced at that time were all spearheaded by him.

In a few more years, he would resign to start an investment fund.

After Xiaomi was founded, the first private equity fund it participated in was one where Director Kou pulled Lei Jun into the partnership. Successively brought in by Director Kou were also Shanda, Ourpalm, Youzu, Rastar, Linekong, Renren, Powerlong...

Chen Guilang would definitely join in the future, but how much he would invest depended on how much support Director Kou showed him over the next few years.

"You're going to develop three games simultaneously?" Director Kou asked.

Chen Guilang gave an indirect answer, "Thank you for your concern, Sir."

Director Kou asked again, "Tackling so many at once, aren't you worried you'll bite off more than you can chew? After all, You-Ke is still just a medium-sized company. The state is supporting domestic games now, but we still hope you can proceed steadily."

Chen Guilang said, "Among the three games, the investment in that single-player one isn't large, with the initial input under 1 million yuan. The other two aren't being developed at the exact same time either. *Future Era* has been in development for almost a year, and *My Own Swordsman* is still in the preparatory stage."

"It's good that you have a comprehensive plan," Director Kou said. "The list for the third batch of 'National Online Game Project Works' will be announced in October. There are 20 domestic games in total, and *Sanguo Sha* has already been selected. You should come in person then."

"I'll definitely be there," Chen Guilang said happily.

Getting on this thing depended not only on the quality of the game itself, but also on whether one's connections were strong enough.

For last year's second batch, *Sanguo Sha* wasn't selected. Sohu's *Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils*, however, was selected just as its development began!

As long as a game made it onto this list, it would receive official support.

Each game would be subsidized with 500,000 to 1 million yuan in R&D funds, and the company's local government would have to provide additional subsidies.

Overseas revenue, including from Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, would enjoy a 13% value-added tax rebate and be eligible for subsidies from the overseas expansion fund.

It would be included in the national key cultural export project catalog. For example, if *Sanguo Sha* were to be published in the United States, You-Ke could send people to the Chinese embassy in the US to seek assistance.

In the future, when the game version number system was implemented, the approval period for games on this list would be cut in half.

Now that *Sanguo Sha* was selected, You-Ke's various policy support applications in Beijing would surely get green-lighted all the way. This included the "three years tax-free, two years half-tax" policy—ByteDance had already gotten it, while You-Ke was still in the application process.

Director Kou added, "Submit all three of your new games to apply for next year's fourth batch list. But only one can be selected, I hope you can understand."

"I understand. The leadership needs to consider the big picture," Chen Guilang said.

With only 20 slots for games each year, they certainly couldn't let Chen Guilang monopolize three of them.

The Publication Administration had to consider how to divide the cake.

Otherwise, if all the slots were taken by large and medium-sized companies, how could they support those small enterprises?

There were even special hidden quotas each year for those fledgling small companies. The Publication Administration would select one or two of the most promising games from all the submissions and subsidize them. Although most of them failed, a single success was a political achievement.

After the conversation ended, Chen Guilang stood up and saw Director Kou off.

To be honest, Chen Guilang had some complaints about the Publication Administration. In every respect, *Sanguo Sha* should have been selected for last year's second batch.

But he hadn't pulled any strings back then. It wasn't until after the second batch was confirmed that Director Kou discovered *Sanguo Sha* had actually sold itself to Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea.

So last winter, Director Kou visited You-Ke for an inspection, which was considered a gesture of his support for *Sanguo Sha*.

That instantly mended his relationship with Chen Guilang.

How do you think Director Kou got such a terrifying network of connections when he later resigned to start a private equity fund?

He had excellent relationships with the bosses of all the major and medium-sized game companies.

Well, alright, there were exceptions.

For instance, to support and protect domestic games, he would deliberately hold up the version numbers for foreign games being imported by certain companies. This created friction with those presidents.

Around noon, Tao Chenggang appeared, beaming with joy. "*Dominion* has been selected for the third batch of the National Online Game Project."

"Congratulations, congratulations. *Sanguo Sha* was selected too," Chen Guilang said with a smile.

If *Dominion* was selected, then *Zhengtu* and *Eudemons Online* were definitely selected as well.

This year's list was worth its weight in gold.

Tao Chenggang sat down assertively, sighing with emotion. "Two or three years ago, I wouldn't have even dared to dream of this. The reason I'm where I am today, brother, is all thanks to your help."

Chen Guilang smiled. "It's because you yourself were bold enough to risk everything to make games. My help was just the icing on the cake."

Tao Chenggang shook his head repeatedly. "Without the game plan you sold me, I never would have made games. I'd probably still be running internet cafes in Longdu."

"Haha, let's not talk about that. We're all brothers here," Chen Guilang said.

Tao Chenggang said, "Shi Yuzhu invited me for drinks, and I've already accepted. He also asked me to invite you. Are you going?"

Chen Guilang said, "Sure. I don't have anything else to do tonight anyway."

The afternoon event was the cosplay competition.

The number of cosplayers who came to compete this year had doubled from last year. They didn't necessarily have to cosplay game characters; in fact, most were anime characters.

The teams representing the major game companies were mostly there for show and generally did not participate in the competition rankings.

Watching the cosplay performance on stage, Chen Guilang asked the You-Ke exhibition manager beside him, "How many tickets have we sold for the *Sanguo Sha* finals?"

The exhibition manager was named Duan Zhixing, a Nanjing University graduate recruited by Qu Guohao.

At this time, there were two major factions within You-Ke.

One was the technical team led by Dong Qianqiu, mainly composed of Peking University graduates, but also including graduates from other Beijing universities. They held an absolute majority in numbers.

The other was the management and operations team led by Qu Guohao. He had brought in more than a dozen old colleagues, mostly graduates from major universities in Jinling. He also absorbed the teams Ao Yanchen and Xie Yang had left behind at You-Ke.

Outside these two factions, there was also the "Future Studio," which was the *Future Era* development team. It reported directly to Chen Guilang.

Future Studio was quite diverse, with people from all over the country. There were veteran professionals poached from Object Software and Pixel Software, newcomers like Feng Ji who had just entered the industry, and even writers like Shuxia Yehou.

Duan Zhixing was not only in charge of this exhibition but also the upcoming *Sanguo Sha* finals.

For this year's finals, they directly rented a large hall in the SNIEC where ChinaJoy was being held. It could accommodate 5,000 spectators!

Duan Zhixing said, "Over 2,700 people have bought tickets online. Through promotions at the expo over the last two and a half days, another 1,200-plus have bought tickets offline. I'll step up the promotion this afternoon. But we might still end up with a few hundred empty seats."

"It's fine, let them be empty if they are," Chen Guilang said, showing his understanding.

The slogan for this year's *Sanguo Sha* National Collegiate League Finals was "One Family: Universities Across the Strait and Three Regions," because university students from Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan would also be participating.

The leaders were paying close attention, as this had political significance!

Director Kou from the Publication Administration and local Shanghai leaders would personally attend the finals. The venue rental fee of 50,000 yuan a day was voluntarily reduced to 30,000 yuan by the local leaders.

Director Kou also helped to keep the reporters attending ChinaJoy around. The number of reporters alone was over a hundred.

Even CCTV and Dragon TV sent reporters to conduct interviews and film.

*Xinwen Lianbo*!

Although it would appear as a news brief of a few seconds, getting on *Xinwen Lianbo* was a rare achievement.

Without the slogan "One Family: Universities Across the Strait and Three Regions," a small-scale esports tournament like this would have no chance of being on CCTV.

After the third day's afternoon activities ended, another 300-plus tickets for the *Sanguo Sha* finals were sold.

Factoring in the seats for leaders and reporters, the 5,000-seat exhibition hall would probably have five or six hundred empty seats.

Tickets were still 30 yuan each.

This time, meals were not included, but each person would receive a T-shirt printed with the *Sanguo Sha* logo and a small souvenir gift.

After calculating all the costs, they would barely break even.

This was because an electronics brand had sponsored them with 300,000 yuan.

The showgirls hired by You-Ke would continue to work until the *Sanguo Sha* finals were over.

That evening, the major game companies packed up and left.

Only the You-Ke team remained.

Shi Yuzhu said, "You've made this quite a big event. I hear even CCTV reporters are coming?"

Chen Guilang smiled. "It's all thanks to Director Kou's favor. I don't have that much influence."

Shi Yuzhu looked at the promotional poster for "One Family: Universities Across the Strait and Three Regions" and asked, "Is it going to be on *Xinwen Lianbo*?"

"I don't know," Chen Guilang replied ambiguously.

"They're here," Shi Yuzhu said.

The drinking party Shi Yuzhu was hosting tonight wasn't just for Chen Guilang and Tao Chenggang.

There were two other people.

One was the president of Perfect World, Chi Yufeng.

The other was the controversial "Red-clothed Hierarch," Zhou Hongyi.

ChinaJoy was an electronics expo, not just a game expo, so it was perfectly normal for Zhou Hongyi to come and promote Qihoo 360 Safeguard.

Qihoo 360 Safeguard had just launched this month, with the slogan "Professionally uninstall rogue software" *side-eye emoji*.

After this guy left Yahoo, he also became an investment partner at IDG. Xunlei was one of the companies he participated in investing in.

"President Chen, President Tao, I've long heard of your great names!"

"You're too kind. It is your name, President Zhou, that is truly renowned."

"Hello, President Chi."

"Hello."

For the past few days, Shi Yuzhu had been inviting people for drinks every night; he was a damn drunkard.

Chen Guilang and the others were the third batch to be invited.

The dinner was at the Shanghai Tang Palace Club, a private club invested in by Stanley Ho. It seemed Mr. Sun Yat-sen's granddaughter also had a stake.

You had to be a member to dine there, and the number of non-member guests could not exceed the capacity of the private room.

This was the first time a country bumpkin like Chen Guilang had come to such a high-class place.

His specific impression was: it was just so-so. But the building and garden were exceptionally beautiful.

(End of this chapter)
